name: Ports
description: What is listening on this computer's TCP ports, with a Kill button. A tool for this computer only, so it doesn't sync.

scripts.kill-port.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Stop whatever is listening on TCP port $1 (lsof on a Mac, lsof or ss on Linux)
case "$1" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "Not a port: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
lsof=/usr/sbin/lsof
[ -x "$lsof" ] || lsof=$(command -v lsof)
if [ -n "$lsof" ]; then
  pids=$("$lsof" -t -nP -iTCP:"$1" -sTCP:LISTEN | grep -vx "$TAILAPPS_PID")
elif command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  pids=$(ss -Hltnp "sport = :$1" 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'pid=[0-9]*' | cut -d= -f2 | sort -u | grep -vx "$TAILAPPS_PID")
else
  echo "Needs lsof or ss to stop a port" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ -z "$pids" ]; then
  echo "Nothing you can stop is listening on port $1" >&2
  exit 1
fi
kill $pids
